question: Which exact 3.1.28 entry points back the Supervisor platform services already recovered on Band 9 3.1.32 (monotonic clock, heap, lseek/mkdir/rmdir/fsync, battery, wake locks, screen state and wake, manual brightness, properties, MiWear link state, LVGL service timer, Bluetooth adapter state), and which earlier ensemble records are wrong?
prototype_hypothesis: Same AAPCS contracts as the Band 9 3.1.32 platform hooks (EVID-PLATFORM-HW-9132-001), called from the UI owner thread; battery uses the ready + snapshot pair.
callsite_evidence: NuttX functions carry their source path in DEBUGASSERT (strings referenced through the 0x2C000000 alias): clock/clock_gettime.c -> 0xC0EA200, vfs/fs_lseek.c -> file_seek 0xC38C1F0 behind lseek 0xC38F272 (fs_getfilep 0xC38BE90, fs_putfilep 0xC38ED98), vfs/fs_mkdir.c -> 0xC39034C, vfs/fs_rmdir.c -> 0xC3906E8, mm_heap/mm_malloc.c -> mm_malloc 0xC121BA4 behind malloc 0xC121DC8, mm_heap/mm_free.c -> mm_free 0xC11EEC0 behind free 0xC11EEE8 (both on the user heap 0x200936A8; kmm_malloc 0xC121E5C / kmm_free 0xC11EEFC use the kernel heap 0x2009359C).
There is no vfs/fs_fsync.c string; fsync 0xC38F958 is fs_getfilep + file_fsync 0xC38A568 (mountpoint ops +36 or driver ioctl 0x50D) + fs_putfilep, -1 plus errno.
clock_gettime masks the clock id with 7, reads the monotonic base for clocks 1/4, adds the realtime offset for 0 and writes {int64 tv_sec, int32 tv_nsec}.
lseek stores the 64-bit offset from r2:r3, loads whence from the first stack argument and returns -1 in r0:r1 on error.
mkdir passes mode (r1) & ~umask to the mountpoint mkdir (ops +0x54); without a mountpoint it reserves a pseudo directory.
struct stat is 96 bytes here (stat pseudo helper 0xC38FD20 and file_fstat 0xC38FE5C clear 96 bytes, st_size at +24), not the 104-byte layout the Supervisor expects, so stat is not recorded.

uv_topic_battery_state_cb 0xC4778E0 (PowerManager, also logs set_battery_state_from_topic_data) sets the charging-ready byte 0x200A22C0 and the level-ready byte 0x200A22C1, the charging flag 0x200A22C4 and the level dword 0x200A22C8; 0xC472230 returns ready-and-ready, 0xC47224C copies the two words to out[0..1]; the BatteryReminder callers 0xC33A0CC / 0xC33D498 read out[1] as the level and the out[0] byte as charging.

PowerManager wakelock_create 0xC47617C logs 'succeeded, levelAndFlags=%lu, tag=%s', stores the tag at +8 and wraps a 'wakelock' screen session at +32; unlike 3.1.32 it does not validate the level and always sets keep-on (+12 = 1). Acquire 0xC47862C counts at +20 and on the first hold calls screen_session_start(s, 1) and, with flag 0x10000000, screen_turn_on("wakelock", 26); 0xC478658 is the timed acquire; release 0xC47870C stops the session on the last release.

MiWearScreen logs __func__ for every session call: screen_session_create 0xC4758EC, start 0xC47595C (tag, handle, auto_stop), stop 0xC4759E8, set_auto_brightness 0xC476020 (status names UNSPECIFIED/ENABLED/DISABLED at 0x2C72DB78, so 2 = DISABLED), set_brightness_value 0xC4760B0, restore_default 0xC47623C, screen_turn_on 0xC478508. The stock alarmclock_screen_dim 0xC23C0D0 runs create -> set_auto_brightness(s, 2) -> set_brightness_value(s, 60) -> start(s, 0).

screen_get_state 0xC4723B8 returns 2 while a keep-on hold is counted (0x200A34B4), otherwise the applied state byte 0x200A34BC; async_apply_screen_state_change 0xC4780E0 names states OFF/AOD/ON (0/1/2) from 0x2C72D790.

property_get 0xC4D2DE8 queries kvdbd over a socket, returns the value length (up to 255 bytes plus NUL) or -22 for a missing key with a NULL default; property_get_int32 0xC4DF244 is property_get(key, buf, NULL) + strtol 0xC114430(buf, &end, 0) returning the default on error or trailing characters; MiWearScreen init 0xC388098 reads persist.screen.auto_brightness / brightness_value with it.

system_all_state getter 0xC38CD4C reads the struct through the pointer 0x200B508C (state 1 = byte +1, get_connect_state) but builds a 256-byte local result (memset 0x100) and memcpy's all 256 bytes into the caller's out buffer on every path (case 15 copies the 255-byte app region string); with a NULL pointer it spins in an empty loop.

lv_timer_create 0xC327D6C inserts into the timer list 0x200A2474 that lv_timer_handler 0xC327EEC (.../lvgl/src/misc/lv_timer.c) walks, stores period +0, last_run +4, callback +8, user_data +12, repeat_count -1 and sets the auto-delete flag; 0xC328054 calls it as (cb, 1300, user_data). lv_timer_del 0xC327ECC removes from the same list, sets timer_deleted and frees through lv_mem_free 0xC327EB4 -> free 0xC11EEE8; lv_timer_handler calls it for auto-delete timers.

bts_adapter_init 0xC53B630 creates the framework Bluetooth client instance (0xC4CC9B0), stores it in g_bt_ins 0x2009CC08 (named by its 'wrong state: g_bt_ins %p' log) and reads the adapter state with bt_adapter_get_state 0xC4C61CC, comparing against 4 (ON); btstack_sdk_init 0xC1D4180 does the same. bt_adapter_get_state is IPC command 27 (0xC4C61AA) returning the state byte, 0 on IPC failure; the existing EVID-O66-ASTROLINK-ABI-001 record for it is confirmed and left unchanged.

Ensemble records refuted: clock_gettime 0xC1BDE54 is a list/semaphore worker, heap_malloc 0xC412894 a C++ copy helper, heap_free 0xC2520C4 a two-argument wrapper around 0xC251C88, lseek 0xC3B82A4 a Bluetooth protocol handler, lv_timer_create 0xC4E10A0 and lv_timer_del 0xC4E1250 thunks, bt_adapter_get_instance 0xC38150C a one-line field store. The Supervisor generated before this review used 0xC4E10A1 as lv_timer_create, 0xC412895 as heap_malloc and 0xC3B82A5 as lseek.
ownership_analysis: Wake-lock objects and brightness sessions are created once per Supervisor slot and kept; wakelock_create and screen_session_create store the tag pointer, so the tag must be static. heap_malloc/heap_free share the user heap. g_bt_ins is owned by the Bluetooth service and read only. Nothing here takes ownership of caller buffers beyond the call.
unsafe_assumptions: system_get_state 0xC38CD4C is not recorded: it writes 256 bytes into its out buffer while the Supervisor passes uint32_t out[2] (a 248-byte stack overrun). system_state 0x200B508C is recorded, so the MiWear link hook stays off until the Supervisor either passes a 256-byte buffer or reads byte +1 through the pointer.

bt_shared_adapter (g_bt_ins 0x2009CC08) is recorded, but the target_config generator only maps bt_adapter_get_instance to the Supervisor; CANOPUS_SUP_BT_SHARED_ADAPTER comes from the Band 11 address header, so the adapter-state hook stays off on this target until codegen maps it. bt_adapter_get_state issues a synchronous IPC to the Bluetooth service.

The vibrator is preset-only: miwear_vibrator_run 0xC47BD9C takes a 12-byte block whose type byte selects one of 35 stock patterns (1..35), with no waveform kind byte or duration; miwear_vibrator_cancel 0xC47BE5C cancels by id. No vibrator_run/vibrator_cancel is recorded, so haptics stays UNSUPPORTED.
wakelock_create accepts any level here and always keeps the screen on; the Supervisor passes level 6, which matches.
stat is not recorded (96-byte struct stat); the Supervisor's opendir + lseek fallback is used.
recommended_probe: all-services-test on Mirage (emulator evidence only), then on a device: battery, wake lock, wake screen, brightness override, property reads and the LVGL service timer.
